precepts.text: The Most High maketh the barren woman to keep house and to be a joyful mother of children.
precepts.point: This is one of many examples in the Bible of our foremothers going through barrenness, and when the Most High was ready he enabled them to conceive. Sisters who have tried for years without children should in patience possess their souls, take comfort of the scriptures, meditate on the foremothers, and believe what the Bible says.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
The angel told the woman plainly, “thou art barren, and bearest not: but thou shalt conceive, and bear a son.” “He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the Lord.” This is one of many examples in the Bible of our foremothers going through barrenness, and when the Most High was ready he enabled them to conceive.

Sisters who have tried for years without children should in patience possess their souls, take comfort of the scriptures, meditate on the foremothers, and believe what the Bible says: he maketh the barren woman a joyful mother of children.

precepts.text: When a man or woman separates themselves to vow a vow of a Nazarite, they are on another level of dedication to the Lord: no wine, no strong drink, no vinegar, no liquor of grapes, nothing made of the vine tree from the kernels even to the husk.
precepts.point: The locks of the Nazarite also witness to who Israel is; the hair of Israel naturally grows into locks.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
The angel commanded the mother herself to “drink not wine nor strong drink, and eat not any unclean thing”, because “the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb”; even in the womb he was to be kept pure. The vow is laid out in Numbers 6: “When either man or woman shall separate themselves to vow a vow of a Nazarite, to separate themselves unto the Lord: He shall separate himself from wine and strong drink, and shall drink no vinegar of wine, or vinegar of strong drink, neither shall he drink any liquor of grapes, nor eat moist grapes, or dried.” Nothing made of the vine tree, “from the kernels even to the husk.” A Nazarite is on another level of dedication to the Lord.

Samson is one of the first examples in scripture of somebody actually living that vow. Understand the difference between a Nazarite and a Nazarene: Christ was a Nazarene because he was from the city of Nazareth, not a Nazarite; he drank wine, and Nazarites could not drink the blood of the grape at all.

precepts.text: All the days of the vow no razor shall come upon his head; he shall be holy and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow, which is why the angel gave Manoah's wife these instructions.
precepts.point: The locks of the Nazarite also witness to who Israel is; the hair of Israel naturally grows into locks.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
“no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb”. That comes straight from the vow: “All the days of the vow of his separation there shall no razor come upon his head: until the days be fulfilled, in the which he separateth himself unto the Lord, he shall be holy, and shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow.” That is why the angel gave Manoah’s wife these instructions; her son’s days of separation would run from the womb, and he would begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.

The locks of the Nazarite also witness to who Israel is: the hair of Israel naturally grows into locks, the locks the vow speaks of.

precepts.text: The angel of the Lord descended, rolled back the stone, and sat upon it; his countenance was like lightning and his raiment white as snow, and for fear of him the keepers did shake and became as dead men.
precepts.point: She repeated the message: the child shall be a Nazarite to God from the womb to the day of his death, and she was to drink no wine nor strong drink nor eat any unclean thing.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
The woman said the man’s “countenance was like the countenance of an angel of God, very terrible”. Verse 3 says it was the angel of the Lord, but he did not tell her, so she was not sure; she only knew his face was terrible like an angel’s. See what an angel’s countenance is: “the angel of the Lord descended from heaven, and came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it. His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow: And for fear of him the keepers did shake, and became as dead men.”

The popular pictures of angels as cute babies with smooth cheeks and little white wings do not match the biblical descriptions at all. Grown men, the keepers at the sepulchre, shook and became as dead men. To see an angel of the Most High was a terrifying sight, not something to jump for joy about, and that is just how Manoah’s wife described the one that came to her.

precepts.text: Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels.
precepts.point: Manoah still did not know that he was an angel of the Lord.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
The angel told Manoah, “if thou wilt offer a burnt offering, thou must offer it unto the Lord.” He knew Manoah might try to offer it up to him, since he appeared like a god, so he directed the offering to the Lord. “Let no man beguile you of your reward in a voluntary humility and worshipping of angels, intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up by his fleshly mind”.

Israel is quick to worship anything that looks like it could be God, because we cannot see the Most High; that is why the scriptures warn against the worshipping of angels. Manoah did not even know he was an angel of the Lord, yet the angel turned the offering to the Lord before the error could be made.

precepts.text: John the revelator, the disciple whom Christ loved, fell down to worship before the feet of the angel, and the angel said, see thou do it not, for I am thy fellowservant and of thy brethren the prophets: worship God.
precepts.point: Manoah still did not know that he was an angel of the Lord.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

precepts.why:
Even John the revelator, the disciple whom Christ loved, made the mistake the angel was guarding Manoah from: “I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things. Then saith he unto me, See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.”

The angel of the Lord did the same with Manoah: “I will not eat of thy bread”, and a burnt offering “thou must offer it unto the Lord.” Angels of the Most High refuse worship and point it to God. Israel is quick to worship anything that looks like it could be God because we cannot see the Most High, so the scripture keeps the line plain: worship God.

points: The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord, and the Lord delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years. This is the pattern of the book of Judges: after Joshua's death Israel went off, and nation after nation was given power over them before the great captivities ever came.

The angel knew Manoah might try to offer it up to him, since he appeared like a god, so he directed the offering to the Lord. Israel is quick to worship anything that looks like it could be God because we cannot see the Most High, which is why the scriptures warn against the worshipping of angels.

points: Manoah asked the angel his name, so that when his sayings came to pass they might do him honour.

points: The angel answered, why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is secret? His name was too wonderful to be uttered to him.

points: Manoah took a kid with a meat offering and offered it upon a rock unto the Lord, and the angel did wondrously: when the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, the angel of the Lord ascended in the flame and went out of their sight.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah and his wife fell on their faces to the ground at the sight. This is the kind of thing Israel was able to see and witness with their own eyes.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: Manoah said to his wife, we shall surely die, because we have seen God. This is a passage the contradictors point to, since the Bible says no man hath seen God; but God here is Elohim, which is plural and speaks of heavenly beings. They saw an angel, not the Most High God.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: His wife reasoned rightly: if the Lord were pleased to kill us, he would not have received a burnt offering and a meat offering at our hands, neither would he have shewed us all these things.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: The woman bare a son and called his name Samson, and the child grew, and the Lord blessed him.

note.label: Judges 13: A Nazarite from the Womb

points: The spirit of the Lord began to move him at times in the camp of Dan between Zorah and Eshtaol; the Most High began to deal with him.
